name: Adam
comments:
Conditions were not great on 20m this afternoon. I could just hear DJ9FM, Willie, but alas, he did not hear me. Maybe I need to peddle harder? 

To top off the poor conditions on 20m we had a storm pass through just before the NET. I thought it was done and dusted, sadly, it was slow moving and another was following behind, causing significant static crashes. 

All was not lost! I did work Phil ZL1PB who had a solid signal. He was no match for the crashes though and I had to cut the QSO short to unplug the antenna(s).

Cheers
Adam, VK4IM

name: Stan
heard40: ZL1TSS ZL3XDJ VK3ACU ZL1PB VK4IM VK6TX VK5AO VK6HRC VK7TA VL2DLF VK4PN VK2GAZ
comments:
Was grand to hear 40 m the best it's been for many a week, at last a clean waterfall with lots of yellow, orange and even a couple of red dotted lines.   If intra-ZL signals remain this good for a while longer, who knows, NZ Net might move to 40 m before Christmas.  The call signs listed in the table show my whole night's work, not just the QRS FFA.  
Don't ya just love that big, old Post Office stamp?  Well done Lance!  (Those who contributed to the table will know what I mean)
caption: Photo showing the driven end of random wire at ZL3TK, Waitarere Beach.  The convenience and efficiency of automatic all-HF-band coupling blows away the doubters and critics.

heard40: VK2KI/P, VK7TO, VK3KLE, VK3TBR, VK1WA, VK3DRQ, VK4PN
comments: Other demands have kept me away from the key of late so it was nice to do some listening again.  I was very, very rusty, slow on the copy, some clumsy mistakes on the send.  Still, nice to hear 7 stations, have QSO's with two.  I was not quick enough to catch Mark, I listened as he concluded a QSO with Lance but when I called Mark had already moved on and I found him a little further down a few moments later and in another QSO.  Thanks Paul and Ian for being patient with me, including my mistakes. I am hoping to be a bit more regular on the CQQRS net going forward.

name: David
comments:
More activity was heard on 40m last night.   No stations were contacted as there was heavy QSB.  
I recorded nothing for 20m last night.  The only stations I could hear were QRQ stations and too fast for me.  
80m appeared very quiet last night.  I did take down some call signs however QSB was heavy so a QSO was not achieved.

name: Willie
qth: JO30WJ - Montabaur - Half way between Frankfurt in the south and Cologne in the north.
comments:
I wanted to do better than the last times and so I took my car to a nearby top of a small hill. Here I set up my gear in a misty and early morning. Outside of the car there was a self build drive-on mount for my mast carrying a 1/4 wave vertical with elevated radials. In the car were the Yaesu 897, my homebrew key, a headphone, batteries and a notebook.
The temperature was ok, as soon as I got inside the car and out of the wind. Then I started calling CQ.

My CQ VK QRS was answered by a station from Belarus, EW3DI, but he was gone before we could exchange reports. The next one was from Russia R2WB. We exchanged reports and I told him, that I was looking for VK.

When ZL1PB called, I first understood DL1... quite common here ;) ... but then, RR, I got it. There still was QRM and QSB, hard conditions for a beginner like me. But we managed to get a valid QSO. Now I am very pleased, that I had the first QSO in the group.
caption: Portable set up in the morning mist.

name: Patrick
comments: I had 4 QSOs on 40m.  So thought I should submit a report to try out the new report form!  I will even try out the new photo capability.  The photo is of my hacksaw sideswiper.  With my sending on this key the spacing between dits and dahs is shorter than it should be, however the Vband decoder still does a good job of reading it, so the sending can't be that bad.  My 4 QSOs were VK2DLF (RSN 592); JF1LXO (RST 439); VK2GAZ (RST 559); and VK3DRQ (RSN 592).  Conditions seemed good though with a little background QRN, hence the 2 assigned in RSN reports.  VK2GAZ was using only 5 watts.

name: Phil
comments: I wasn't able to put my aerial out under the carport last night due to the weather (I need to leave the door slightly open to get the cable inside) so I listened to the Ironstone range SDR. I copied three stations reasonably well (readability 4 - 5 due to atmospheric noise and fading) and copied the odd word from the faster stations.

name: Wayne
comments: Again the bands were very noisy due to the proliferation of thunderstorms across the island. Nothing was heard on 20m. Some success on 40m with one local and several eastern island stations. I heard Mark trying to work Peter VK6NQL but Mark was barely readable.

name: Lance
comments:
I didn't manage much time on the air on Tuesday, so was fortunate to catch Mark, 2KI, for a brief ragchew at the start of the evening.

Having checked the space weather forecast and noted the solar flux under 100, I wasn't expecting too many stations to make it down to southern Tas.  Thus anticipating a quite band I elected to use my old TS-520S which has no CW filters.  How wrong I was.  A low SFI (Solar Flux Index) does of course result in lower signal strengths, but also lower QRN resulting in an improved SNR.  I couldn't tune anywhere in the vicinity of our COA without a few stations operating in my passband, both local (VK/ZL) and many VA stations.  It was a good opportunity to exercise that filter between my ears, as well as trying to copy two stations at the same time.
caption: My trusty TS-520S.  A beautiful rig to operate, but the lack of narrow filters can be a challenge on a busy band.

name: Daniel
comments: There were several weak signals when I tuned in with a single clear signal from Ron, VK6KHZ.  However I was tempted by the low, but readable, signal from VK3DRQ to try for my first interstate contact.  Unfortunately after sending my reply QSB set in and I was not able to read any response.  By the time the signal improved VK3DRQ was calling CQ again.  Ron had also stopped transmitting and I had no response calling CQ.  Oh well there will be another opportunity!
